textRun.content: What should the robot learn from a failed lift?
The same task can require different kinds of learning.
The cube was positioned differently this time.
Correct the estimate for this attempt.
This cube is heavier than it looks.
Remember its corrected mass for the next attempt.
The question is when should a lesson stay specific to one object, and when should it apply to others?
The same mistake occurs on many objects.
Improve the shared estimator, model or skill.
At train, the policy is fed the true object mass such that it leans the behavior to adapt.
Separatly we train a mass estimator that guesses the mass before interaction. (vision -> estimated mass)
At deployment we feed the mass estimate and policy performs.
Current work: estimate mass for a fixed policy
Top-down pick and lift. A fixed RL policy receives state and an estimated object mass.
Converted to weight for the policy
Fixed material and density; predict mass from appearance.
Test on held-out cube sizes within the sampled range.
One material; fixed density, friction and camera. Test sizes lie within the training range.
Next challenge: 1-two cubes can look the same but have different masses.
2-estimates being refined as model success & fails.
Result: policy with estimator running in sim
One initial image → one mass estimate → a fixed policy → pick-and-lift execution.
Example run: 125.0 g actual → 121.24 g estimated; cube lifted and held.
The estimate stays fixed pre episode. We have not yet measured whether it improves the lift.
Intermediate settings mixed success and failure.
More data could map success probabilities;
that alone does not explain each failure.
Also mass/friction must still be inferred. Which is not possible at deployment
Both failure case fails to grasp where cube goes out reach. They are different in the sense that red had many tries to grasp.
What we tried: two ways we explored failures
Both showed patterns, but neither yet identifies the cause of an individual failure.
Motion, relative pose, finger forces and actions
Green = success; red = failure across starts
Reuse past data and policies when learning new tasks.
Use summaries of robot experience for LLM explanations.
Train on generated failures to detect and explain them.
Next steps: study how learning systems improve
Two valuable directions alongside the proposed robot experiments.
Read Xie & Finn on lifelong robotic RL.
How can a robot reuse past experience
when it learns a new task?
Could they help explain failures and
choose what the robot should learn?
Reading next: Lifelong Robotic RL by Retaining Experiences — Xie & Finn
Result: motion groups did not explain failure causes
We tried to identify failure types by grouping recorded motion and pose.
They did not match the failure types we wanted to identify.
Identify why a lift failed, and test whether the cause is familiar or new.
Motion / pose / force history → PCA + k-means → 2 candidate behavior groups
Then: test whether a better estimate improves the lift
Proposed pilot: one cube appearance, varied mass. Keep friction and policy fixed.
Does giving the true mass improve the lift?
Can contact and motion signals reveal mass?
Give the policy the true mass
Allow the same amount of interaction. Compare mass error, successful lifts and drops.
Train the updater in simulation. At deployment, keep its weights fixed and update the estimate.
